note_on_method: This is a state page, so most of it is a claim about coverage rather than about a court. Where it describes a place, the source is that operator's own publication - the City of St. George's pickleball page, Lehi City Parks' parks page, and the City of Orem's page for each park. Where it describes what is missing, it names the park and says why it is not here, because 'not listed' and 'does not exist' are different things and a reader deserves to know which one they are reading. Statements about cities that have not been published are statements about a reading list on one day, not about those cities' courts. This page exists because Lehi and Orem were published on 7 September 2026, giving Utah three verified cities. Nobody working on this has played on any court in Utah.

slots.coverage:
Utah has twenty-nine counties. This page covers three cities in two of them.

Twelve venues, eighty-four courts, three municipal operators. Washington County holds three of the venues and forty-six of the courts, all inside St. George. Utah County holds nine venues and thirty-eight courts: six venues and sixteen courts in Lehi, three venues and twenty-two courts in Orem. Every venue is run by a city parks department, and not one private club, school, church gym, gated community or commercial facility appears. That is a statement about who writes court counts down rather than about where pickleball in Utah is played.

A venue publishes when its operator states a court count and an address that resolves, a city when three or more of its venues do, and a state when three of its cities do. St. George was verified first; Lehi and Orem were verified together in one batch, all three read on 7 September 2026, and Utah reached three cities when they did.

The three cities arrived by three different kinds of document, and the differences matter more than the totals. St. George publishes one pickleball page that ends in a four-line list under the heading "City of St. George Pickleball Courts" - "Little Valley / 2149 Horseman Park Drive / Courts:  33", "Vernon Worthen / 300 S. 400 E. / Courts: 6", "Bloomington Park / 650 Man O War Road / Courts: 7", "Ledges / ? / Courts: 4" - and fills the rest of the page with the programme run on those courts: a 2025 schedule of leagues and tournaments, a check-in rule, a reservation link and an article dated 19 August 2020. Lehi publishes one parks page, "Welcome to Lehi City Parks", that lists every park under "RESERVABLE PAVILIONS" or "NON-RESERVABLE PARKS" with an "Address:" line and an amenity sentence in which the City counts what it has: "Playground, restrooms, 2 pickleball courts, 2 half basketball courts, soccer fields, and a fire pit." Orem publishes one page per park with a "Location:" line and an amenity list, and states its count twice on each page - "12 Pickleball Courts (6 Courts reservable, 6 Courts open for public use)" in Hillcrest's list, then "6 Pickleball courts can be reserved for private use" below it. Many of the published addresses are Utah grid lines - "650 E 1400 S", "300 S. 400 E.", "484 South 1915 West" - a number standing where a street name would, written by the operator without a city or a postcode, and a resolver finds each of them as written.

What the three cities refuse is part of the record and is named rather than dropped. St. George prints "?" where Ledges' address should be, so four stated courts are not placed. Lehi counts courts at eleven parks and this site can place six: Shadow Ridge, four courts at "3050 W. Traverse Mountain Blvd"; Salix, four at "3109 W. Allred Dr."; South Creek, one at "1987 West 1450 South"; and Spring Creek, three at "2108 S Bullrush Pkwy", all carry addresses that neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap resolves as the City writes them. Northridge's "a pickleball court" is an article rather than a number, and its address fails as well. Gateway Park says "pickleball" and never counts. Orem's Cascade Park carries "Pickleball/Tennis Courts" and no number, and its page answered 404 on the day. Sixteen stated courts across the state wait on an address - as many as Lehi publishes - and three more parks wait on a number.

Beyond the three cities, nothing in Utah is published. Salt Lake City, Provo, West Valley City, Sandy, Ogden and the rest of the state have no verified file behind this page, which is a statement about a reading list rather than about their courts. No county parks department appears either. Washington County's page is a St. George page under a county heading, and Utah County's is Lehi and Orem under another; both say so in their own words.
slots.seasonality:
The three Utah operators state almost nothing about seasons, and this page will not supply the missing part from memory. What they do state falls into three kinds: a schedule that moves with the calendar, a season that belongs to something other than a court, and one word about lights.

St. George's schedule is the calendar. The City's "St. George Pickleball Program Schedule / 2025" for Little Valley runs Winter League from 6 January to early March on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday mornings from 9:30 to 11:30 a.m. and evenings from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m., Wednesdays to 9:30, each session reserving "9-32 (24 courts)". Spring League repeats the pattern from 24 March into May with mornings from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m. Two tournaments, the Rock N Roll on 6 to 8 February and the Southern Shootout on 2 to 5 April, take "All 33 Courts" from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. The City names five leagues in all - Winter, Spring, Summer, Endless Summer and Fall - so the programme runs the year round, and it adds that "Times may change based on participation numbers". The schedule is dated 2025 and was read in September 2026, so it is the shape of the year rather than this year's calendar. It says nothing about weather, and although it runs league play to 9:30 p.m. in January, the City never writes the word lights, so lighting at Little Valley is recorded as not stated rather than inferred from a timetable. Nothing at Vernon Worthen or Bloomington carries a time of any kind.

Orem's one season belongs to a splash pad and a sledding hill. Hillcrest's page prints "Hours of Operations: Monday-Saturday from 10:00am-8:00pm" under the heading "Splash Pad Hours", beside "Concession will start June 10th from 10:00am-8:00pm", and the next paragraph says "The Splash Pad is open seasonally from Memorial Day at 10:00am to Labor Day at 8pm. After Labor Day, it is closed until the following Memorial Day." Those are the splash pad's hours and its season; nothing on the page ties them to the twelve courts, so court hours at Hillcrest stay unstated and the order of those lines is asserted on every build. Sharon Park's page says that "In the winter, Sharon Park is often used for tubing and sledding. In the summer, it's a nice shady retreat for families" - the one sentence in verified Utah that names both seasons, and it is about the park rather than its six courts.

Lehi states no hours for any court. The one "Hours:" line on its parks page, "Open until dusk", belongs to Lehi Sports Park, where the City counts four tennis courts and no pickleball.

Put together, the evening picture across the state, on what can be verified, is one venue. Bonneville Park in Orem carries the amenity line "Four Lighted Pickleball Courts", and the word "Lighted" is the whole of the evidence. No Utah operator states a lighting negative, so the other eleven venues and eighty courts are recorded as lighting not stated, which means nobody has said, not that the courts are dark. South Creek's "lighting" and Gateway's "park lights" in Lehi sit at refused parks and name no court; Centennial's "pavilion lighting" lights the pavilion. Lit courts are what make play after dark possible - reasoning rather than data, and the one sentence about evenings written here without a source.

The indoor count is zero because the indoor question is unanswered, not because it is answered no. No Utah operator uses the word indoor or outdoor of a court, and a lighted court is not the word outdoor, so the indoor and outdoor breakdowns stay empty for every city, and no indoor, outdoor, lights or free filter page exists anywhere in the state. Rain, heat, snow and summer closures are not mentioned by any of the three, and until one writes something down this section stays as short as it is.
slots.notable:
Little Valley Pickleball Complex in St. George is the largest verified pickleball site in Utah, at thirty-three courts, and it holds more than a third of everything published in the state. It is the one Utah venue published as a dedicated pickleball facility rather than a park: the City heads it "Little Valley Pickleball Complex", numbers its courts on a schedule, reserves "9-32 (24 courts)" for league sessions and "All 33 Courts" for tournaments, keeps an attendant - "Players, please check in with the attendant or instructor to determine if courts are available during the St. George Pickleball programs" - and offers a "Reserve a Pickleball Court" link. It is also the one venue in the state with a stated price. The City's 2020 article says "When courts are vacant the public readily takes advantage of them - free of charge", and the same article says the complex was chosen as "Public Facility of the Year" by the Professional Pickleball Registry and was then "home to 24 well-maintained courts". Thirty-three is the current list's figure, and it is what publishes.

Vernon Worthen Park, six courts at 300 S. 400 E. near the centre of St. George, is where the City says its programme began: "In 2012, Wayne Bullock established the first pickleball program for the City of St. George on four permanent and two temporary courts at Vernon Worthen Park", and the ladder-league format devised there is one "the USA Pickleball Association contacted Bullock for permission to adopt". Its count carries a recheck, because the City's six replaced an imported seven, and a count that has changed once is watched. Bloomington Park's seven courts on Man O War Road come with a name, an address and a number and nothing else.

Hillcrest Park in Orem, twelve courts at 650 E 1400 S, is the largest set in Utah County and the one venue in the state whose operator writes down how a busy court changes hands. Six courts "can be reserved for private use" through the City's online link; the other six "are for public use and will be held to the standard of using the 'Paddle Rotation System'" - waiting players rack a paddle per player on the next open rack, and "When a game is finished players announce 'Open Court' and the court vacated for the players with paddles on the rack." Tournaments and pickleball events go through the City at (801) 229-7154.

Bonneville Park in Orem is the one lit venue in Utah, on the word "Lighted" in "Four Lighted Pickleball Courts", and the City's description calls them "the four new Pickleball courts". Sharon Park's six courts at 600 N 300 E carry the state's plainest booking rule, printed in brackets on the count line: "(we currently ONLY reserve pickleball courts for the city's tournaments, not for any other private use)". Outside a City tournament they are walk-on.

Lehi's notable venue is Holbrook Farms Park, six courts on Drexler Drive in the north-west of the city, the largest count the City states at any of its parks, beside a large pavilion the City calls a "Food Truck Alley". Watercress Park is worth a line for what it counts separately - "8 Horseshoe pits, 2 pickleball courts, 1 tennis court" - so its two courts are not lines on the tennis court. Centennial Park's "1 pickleball court" is the smallest published count in the state and a digit, which is why it publishes when Northridge's "a pickleball court" does not.

The notable venues that are not published deserve exactness. Ledges in St. George has four stated courts and "?" for an address, and the question mark is asserted on every build so that the day the City fills it in, the venue is read again. Shadow Ridge and Salix in Lehi have four stated courts each at addresses neither resolver finds. Cascade Park in Orem carries "Pickleball/Tennis Courts", which is a label and not a count.

Price is stated at one venue in twelve. Little Valley is free when vacant in the City's words. Lehi's "All other amenities are open to the public" is about access rather than cost, and Orem's reservation rules are about who may book, not what it costs. Fifty-one of the eighty-four courts carry no price either way and are recorded as unknown, not as free.
slots.growth:
Nothing in Utah is published as growth, and this page will not describe it as growth on its own authority. No Utah operator prints a construction date, a bond, a planned court or a count history. What the three Cities print is one word, two figures six years apart, a set of reservation rules and a programme, and each says something if it is read to its edge and not past it.

The word is "new". Bonneville Park's page invites the reader to "enjoy a game of Pickleball on one of the four new Pickleball courts", and its amenity list says "Four Lighted Pickleball Courts". The City does not date them, so "new" is published as the City's adjective and nothing more.

The two figures are St. George's. The City's article dated 19 August 2020 says "The Little Valley Pickleball complex is home to 24 well-maintained courts", and the City's undated current list says "Courts:  33". The same article puts the 2012 programme at Vernon Worthen on "four permanent and two temporary courts", and the current list says six. The difference is not read here as an expansion, because the City never says one happened; the current count publishes and the dated one is printed as what the venue was. A dated record that describes itself as history does not contradict a current list, and both sentences are asserted, so if the City revises either, the build stops and the reasoning is re-read.

The reservation rules are Orem's, and they describe a city organising demand rather than merely housing it. Hillcrest's twelve courts are split six reservable through an online link and six on the paddle rotation; Sharon's six are reserved "ONLY" for the City's tournaments; the City takes tournament and event enquiries by phone. St. George's programme is the older one: five named leagues, youth and adult academies, clinics, tournaments and a Tennis and Pickleball Head Pro, with a protective rule beside them - "Please report non-city / unauthorized clinics, lessons, tournaments, or camps to the Parks Department" - and non-City events required to hold a court reservation and possibly a special event permit. Lehi has no programme on its page at all. Its courts are amenities in a sentence, and its one rule is that "Reservations are for pavilion use only. All other amenities are open to the public."

The arrangement of courts is stated by one park. Watercress in Lehi counts "2 pickleball courts, 1 tennis court" as separate things. Bloomington's seven and Olympic's three are odd numbers for a court block and neither City says how they are laid out, and no operator in Utah uses the word dedicated, permanent, portable or shared of a court. Whether any court in the state is lined onto tennis is unknown, and this page leaves it unknown.

What would change this page most is not construction but a record. Sixteen stated courts wait behind five addresses - Ledges' question mark in St. George, and Shadow Ridge, Salix, South Creek and Spring Creek in Lehi - and a resolvable address for any of them promotes it the day it appears. Three parks wait on a number: Northridge and Gateway in Lehi and Cascade in Orem. Two imported rows claim Sharon Park's slug, and the second waits on a written resolution. Outside the three cities the queue is the rest of the state. Every St. George, Lehi and Orem page this state page rests on is snapshotted into the repository that builds it and re-asserted on every build, so if St. George fills in Ledges' address, Lehi moves a park between its two lists, or Orem moves the splash pad's hours under the pickleball block, the build fails and someone reads the page again.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Utah?
faqs.a: Nobody can tell you honestly, and this page will not pretend to. What has been checked is 84 courts across twelve venues in three cities - St. George with 46, Orem with 22, Lehi with 16 - each with a named source and a date. The three Cities' own pages name eight more parks that fail on an address or a missing number, five of them holding sixteen stated courts.

Because three is how many have an operator that states a count and an address for three or more venues on a page we can read and snapshot. Salt Lake City, Provo, West Valley City, Sandy, Ogden and the rest of the state have no verified file behind this page, which says nothing about their courts and everything about a reading list on one day.

faqs.q: Where can I play indoors in Utah?
faqs.a: On no verified court. None of the three operators uses the word indoor or outdoor of a pickleball court, so every one of the 84 courts is recorded as neither rather than as outdoor, and no indoor or outdoor filter page exists for any Utah city. A lighted court at Bonneville is not the word outdoor, and a park amenity sentence does not say which way a court faces the sky.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Utah?
faqs.a: Stated at one venue. The City of St. George's 2020 article says of Little Valley that "When courts are vacant the public readily takes advantage of them - free of charge", with courts reserved for City programmes on a published schedule. Lehi's "All other amenities are open to the public" is not a price, and no Orem page states one, so the other eleven venues are recorded as unknown.

One venue, four courts: Bonneville Park in Orem, whose amenity line is "Four Lighted Pickleball Courts". No other Utah operator writes the word for a court, and none writes a negative, so the other eighty courts are recorded as lighting not stated. St. George schedules league play to 9:30 p.m. in January at Little Valley, which is a timetable fact and not a lighting answer.

faqs.q: What is the biggest pickleball site in Utah?
faqs.a: Little Valley Pickleball Complex in St. George, at thirty-three courts on the City's current list, a programmed facility with an attendant and a reservation link. Hillcrest Park in Orem follows at twelve, then Bloomington Park in St. George at seven, and a group of sixes: Vernon Worthen in St. George, Sharon Park in Orem and Holbrook Farms Park in Lehi.

faqs.q: Can I book a court anywhere in Utah?
faqs.a: At two published venues. St. George offers a "Reserve a Pickleball Court" link for Little Valley and asks players to "contact Parks to make a court reservation at 435-627-4530". Orem reserves six of Hillcrest's twelve courts "for private use" through an online link. Sharon Park is reserved only for City tournaments, Lehi's reservations "are for pavilion use only", and Bonneville states no rule either way.

All three cities' pages were read on 7 September 2026. Each is a static web page that changes without notice, so each is snapshotted into the repository that builds these pages and re-asserted on every build. If St. George supplies an address for Ledges, Lehi rewrites a count in an amenity sentence, or Orem moves Hillcrest's splash-pad hours under its pickleball block, the build fails and the page is read again.
